chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abd al-A'la, freed slave of the progeny of Sam, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The first pigeon that was in Mecca was a pigeon of Ismail (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.آلِ سَامٍ: Family/progeny of Sam (Shem), son of Prophet Nuh (Noah); a tribal designation indicating lineage
key_terms.حَمَام: Pigeon/dove; here referring specifically to a domesticated or kept pigeon, not a wild bird
key_terms.مَكَّة: Mecca; the sacred city containing the Ka'ba, center of Islamic pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the first pigeon in Mecca?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) stated that the first pigeon in Mecca belonged to Prophet Ismail (peace be upon him). This tradition connects the sacred history of Mecca with the lineage of Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail, who built the Ka'ba in Mecca. The hadith is found in a chapter dedicated to the permissibility and virtues of keeping pigeons, and by attributing the first Meccan pigeon to Ismail, it lends a sacred legitimacy to the keeping of these birds near holy places.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin usman, form Abdul A’ala, a slave of the progeny of Sam who sai,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying that: ‘The first pigeon which was at Makkah was a pigeon of Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-‘ Ala’ Mawla’ Ale Sam who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
The first pigeon in Makkah was the pigeon of Tsma‘il ‘Alayhi al-Salam.’”
